title: Who was America's first murderer?
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck discuss John Billington, a Mayflower passenger and Plymouth Colony settler often cited as America's first murderer. They cover the Mayflower voyage myth versus the reality, the "strangers" who were not Puritan separatists, William Bradford's Mourt's Relation and his own journal as promotional and self-serving accounts, the Billington family's troubles (mutiny, musket incident, the lost son John Jr. found with help from Massasoit, Eleanor and Dorcas's punishments), and the 1600s-era sexual crimes recorded in colony records. The episode ends with Billington shooting seventeen-year-old John Newcomen, who had been poaching on his land, with a blunderbuss; Newcomen died of infection days later, and Governor Bradford ordered Billington's execution. The hosts close with a listener mail about accidentally eating cherry hookah tobacco in brownies and nicotine poisoning.

segments.title: Opening banter and Mayflower movie idea
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about Schoolhouse Rock's Mayflower song and why no realistic Mayflower film has been made, touching on Master and Commander and Peter Weir.

segments.title: Pilgrims, strangers, and the myth of Plymouth
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the Pilgrim story was shaped by promotional accounts meant to attract investors, and introduce the 'strangers' who were not Puritan separatists, including Catholics, sailors and others.

segments.title: John Billington and his family
segments.summary: The Billington family is introduced as troublemakers in the eyes of Governor Bradford: the mutiny, the musket shot aboard ship near gunpowder, John Jr.'s wandering and rescue with Massasoit's help, and Billington's run-ins with Miles Standish and the Lyford conspiracy.

segments.title: Eleanor and Dorcas Billington punishments
segments.summary: Eleanor Billington was put in stocks and fined for slander, and granddaughter Dorcas was sentenced to whipping. The hosts note descendants of the Billingtons today.

segments.title: Sexual crimes and punishments in early Plymouth
segments.summary: The hosts describe recorded bestiality, sodomy and rape cases in the colony and the punishments, such as hanging, whipping, stocks and hot irons, noting these were recorded but not promoted.

segments.title: The killing of John Newcomen
segments.summary: Billington shoots seventeen-year-old poacher John Newcomen with a blunderbuss after finding him on his land; Newcomen dies days later of infection. Governor Bradford ordered Billington's execution, and Bradford's own account shaped the historical record.

segments.title: Closing remarks and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts suggest listeners search for more on America's first murderer and encourage Billington descendants to write in; a Stuff from the Future promo follows.

segments.title: Listener mail: nicotine poisoning from brownies
segments.summary: Aaron writes about eating cherry hookah tobacco mixed into brownies baked by his roommate, leading to nicotine poisoning, vomiting, and a hospital visit; he urges people to call poison control.
